'''Bernhard Minnigerode''' (10 August 1837 – 15 August 1896) was a German mathematician, mineralogist and Alpine climber. His name, together with [[Franz Ernst Neumann]], is associated with [[Curie's principle]] which is also named the Neumann–Minnigerode–Curie principle.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brandmüller |first1=J. |title=An extension of the Neumann–Minnigerode–Curie principle |journal=Computers & Mathematics with Applications |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=12 |issue=1–2 |year=1986 |doi=10.1016/0898-1221(86)90143-4 |pages=97–100 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Brandmüller |first1=J. |chapter=An extension of the Neumann–Minnigerode–Curie principle |title=Symmetry: Unifying Human Understanding |editor-last1=Hargittai |editor-first1=István |publisher=Pergamon Press |location=New York |isbn=978-0-08-033986-3|pages=97–100 |year=1986}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Lalena |first1=John N. |last2=Cleary |first2=David A. |last3=Duparc |first3=Olivier B. M. Hardouin |title=Principles of inorganic materials design |date=2020 |publisher=Wiley |location=Hoboken, NJ, USA |isbn=9781119486831 |pages=8,412 |edition=Third}}</ref>

==Career==

Minnigerode was born on 10 August 1837 in [[Darmstadt]]. Minnigerode was a student of Neumann at the [[University of Göttingen]] and gained his PhD with a study of heat conduction in crystals in 1862. Subsequently he moved to the [[University of Greifswald]] and was appointed an associate professor of mathematics in 1874 and a full professor in 1885.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Tobies |first1=Renate |last2=Pakis |first2=Valentine A. |title=Felix Klein: visions for mathematics, applications, and education |date=2021 |publisher=Birkhäuser |location=Cham |isbn=978-3-030-75784-7 |page=95}}</ref> Minnigerode's work spanned mathematics, physics, mineralogy and crystallography. 

In 1884 Minnigerode studied the derivation of the [[Physical crystallography before X-rays#Elastic properties|elastic constants of crystals]], and stated the general relation between the physical characteristics and the symmetry of crystals: "Physically speaking, crystals have all the symmetrical properties of their form; some of the physical properties, however, have still higher symmetry."<ref name=Katzir2004>{{cite journal |last1=Katzir |first1=Shaul |title=The emergence of the principle of symmetry in physics |journal=Historical Studies in the Physical and Biological Sciences |date=September 2004 |volume=35 |issue=1 |pages=35–65 |doi=10.1525/hsps.2004.35.1.35}}</ref><ref name=Minnigerode1884>{{cite journal |last1=Minnigerode |first1=B. |title=Untersuchungen über die Symmetrieverhältnisse und die Elasticität der Krystalle |trans-title=Investigation of the symmetry relations and elasticity of crystals |journal=Nachrichten von der Königl. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften und der Georg-Augusts-Universität zu Göttingen |year=1884 |pages=195–226, 374–384, 488–492 |url=https://eudml.org/doc/180022 |access-date=30 March 2025 |language=German}}</ref>{{rp|218}}

In the same three-part paper Minnigerode also derived the 32 [[Crystallographic point group|crystal classes]] (point groups) using [[group theory]] and stated "The symmetry group of a crystal is a subgroup of the symmetry groups of all the physical phenomena which may possibly occur in that crystal."<ref>{{cite book |last1=Shubnikov |first1=A. V. |last2=Kopt︠s︡ik |first2=V. A. |title=Symmetry in science and art |date=1974 |publisher=Plenum Press |location=New York |isbn=0306307596 |translator-last1=Archard |translator-first1=G. D. |editor-last1=Harker |editor-first1=David |url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_0306307596/page/n5/mode/2up |access-date=28 April 2025 |page=334 |journal=<!-- Citation Bot should not be adding a journal to a book citation as it leads to the following error: "{{cite book}}: |journal= ignored"--> |volume=<!-- Citation Bot should not be adding a journal field to a book citation--> |issue=<!-- Citation Bot should not be adding an issue field to a book citation-->}}</ref>  However, in a letter to [[Arthur Moritz Schoenflies]] dated 21 October 1890, [[Evgraf Fedorov]] claimed that the credit for discovering the 32 crystal classes should go to his countryman [[Axel Gadolin]] and not to Minnigerode.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Burckhardt |first1=J. J. |title=Der Briefwechsel von E.S. von Fedorow Und A. Schoenflies, 1889—1908 |trans-title=The correspondence of E.S. von Fedorow and A. Schoenflies, 1889—1908 |journal=Archive for History of Exact Sciences |volume=7 |issue=2 |year=1971 |pages=91–141 |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/41133319 |access-date=2 August 2025 |language=German |jstor=41133319 |doi=10.1007/bf00411807|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Authier |first1=A. |year=2013 |title=Early days of x-ray crystallography |series=International Union of Crystallography Texts on Crystallography |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford |isbn=9780198754053 |doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199659845.001.0001 |page=396}}</ref> Gadolin's method was based on [[stereographic projection]] rather than group theory, and it was not until the work of [[Andreas Speiser]] in the 1920s that it was recognised that it is exactly the group properties that make symmetry significant for crystals.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Hoddeson |editor1-first=Lillian |editor2-last=Braun |editor2-first=Ernest |editor3-last=Teichmann |editor3-first=Jürgen |editor4-last=Weart |editor4-first=Spencer |title=Out of the crystal maze: chapters from the history of solid state physics |date=1992 |page=20 |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=New York |isbn=0-19-505329-X |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WCpPPHhMdRcC |access-date=29 March 2025}}</ref>

In 1886 Minnigerode extended his symmetry method from elasticity to [[Physical crystallography before X-rays#Thermal conduction|thermal conduction in crystals]].<ref name=Minnigerode1886>{{cite journal |last1=Minnigerode |first1=B. |title=Ueber Wärmeleitung in Krystallen |trans-title=About heat conduction in crystals |journal=Neues Jahrbuch für Mineralogie, Geologie und Paläontologie |year=1886 |volume=1 |pages=1–13 |url=https://archive.org/details/neuesjahrbuchfrm18861leon/page/n25/mode/2up |access-date=21 March 2025 |language=German}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lalena |first1=John N. |title=From quartz to quasicrystals: probing nature's geometric patterns in crystalline substances |journal=Crystallography Reviews |date=April 2006 |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=125–180 |doi=10.1080/08893110600838528 |bibcode=2006CryRv..12..125L }}</ref>{{rp|145–146}} According to Shaul Katzir, a historian of science, "This was the earliest application of a rigorous argument of symmetry in physics beyond elasticity."<ref name=Katzir2004/>{{rp|52}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Katzir |first1=Shaul |title=The beginnings of piezoelectricity: a study in mundane physics |date=2006 |publisher=Springer |location=Dordrecht |isbn=978-1-4020-4669-8}}</ref>{{rp|88}} In 1887 Minnigerode published the first written statement of the Neumann–Minnigerode–Curie symmetry principle.<ref name=Minnigerode1887>{{cite journal |last1=Minnigerode |first1=B. |title=Untersuchungen über die Symmetrieverhältnisse der Krystalle |trans-title=Investigation of the symmetry relations of the crystal |journal=Neues Jahrbuch für Mineralogie, Geologie und Paläontologie |year=1887 |volume=5 |pages=145–166 |url=https://archive.org/details/neuesjahrbuchfr83unkngoog/page/144/mode/2up |access-date=21 March 2025 |language=German}}</ref> A later reviewer commented on Minnigerode's paper: "His discussion, while highly mathematical, is elegant and brief."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Swartz |first1=C. K. |title=Proposed classification of crystals based on the recognition of seven fundamental types of symmetry |journal=Geological Society of America Bulletin |date=1 January 1909 |volume=20 |issue=1 |pages=369–398 |doi=10.1130/gsab-20-369 |bibcode=1909GSAB...20..369S }}</ref>

In the 1880s [[Arthur Moritz Schoenflies]] was using group theory in his studies of crystallographic [[space group]]s. His derivation of the 230 space groups was published in 1894 and tended to obscure Minnigerode's earlier contributions.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Scholz |first1=Erhard |author-link=Erhard Scholz |title=Symmetrie, Gruppe, Dualität: Zur Beziehung zwischen theoretischer Mathematik und Anwendungen in Kristallographie und Baustatik des 19. Jahrhunderts |date=1989 |publisher=Birkhäuser Basel |location=Basel |isbn=978-3-0348-9971-0 |pages=110–111 |language=German |trans-title=Symmetry, group, duality: On the relationship between theoretical mathematics and applications in crystallography and statics in the 19th century}}</ref>

Minnigerode died in [[Špindlerův Mlýn]] in the area of the [[Giant Mountains]] on 15 August 1896.

==Publications==

* 1862: PhD thesis: Über Wärmeleitung in Krystallen [On heat conduction in crystals]<ref>{{cite thesis |last1= Minnigerode |first1=Bernhard |title= Über Wärmeleitung in Krystallen |trans-title=On heat conduction in crystals |language=German |degree=PhD |publisher=Druck der Dieterichschen Univ.-Buchdruckerei |location=Göttingen |year=1862 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6fSNOsJNpmoC |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref>
* 1873: Paper introducing the [[Rounding#Rounding to the nearest integer|nearest integer]] algorithm using [[continued fraction]]s<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Minnigerode |first1=B. |title=Über eine neue Methode, die Pellsche Gleichung aufzulösen |trans-title=About a new method to solve Pell's equation |language=German |journal=Nachrichten von der Königl. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften und der Georg-Augusts-Universität zu Göttingen |year=1873 |issue=23 |pages=619–652 |url=https://archive.org/details/nachrichtengott1873/page/618/mode/2up |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Kalle |first1=Charlene |last2=Sélly |first2=Fanny M. |last3=Thuswaldner |first3=Jörg M. |date=10 December 2024 |title=A finiteness condition for complex continued fraction algorithms |eprint=2406.18689 |class=math.NT}}</ref>
* 1873: Paper on [[quadratic form]]s with [[complex number|complex]] coefficients<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Minnigerode |first1=B. |title=Ueber die Vertheilung der quadratischen Formen mit complexen Coefficienten und Veränderlichen in Geschlechter |trans-title=On the distribution of quadratic forms with complex coefficients and variables in families |journal=Nachrichten von der Königl. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften und der Georg-Augusts-Universität zu Göttingen |year=1873 |pages=160–180 |url=http://eudml.org/doc/179602 |language=German |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref> 
* 1884: Derivation of the 32 [[Crystallographic point group|crystal classes]] using [[group theory]]<ref name=Minnigerode1884/> [http://eudml.org/doc/180034 part II] [https://eudml.org/doc/180042 part III] <ref>{{cite book |last1=Lima-de-Faria |first1=J. |title=Historical atlas of crystallography |date=1990 |publisher=Published for International Union of Crystallography by Kluwer Academic Publishers |location=Dordrecht; Boston |isbn=079230649X |url=https://archive.org/details/historicalatlaso0000unse_p0f2/page/10/mode/2up |url-access=registration |page=10 |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref>
* 1886: Paper on [[Physical crystallography before X-rays#Thermal conduction|heat conduction in crystals]] making use of symmetry considerations<ref name=Minnigerode1886/>
* 1887: Paper in which the Neumann–Minnigerode–Curie principle is formally stated<ref name=Minnigerode1887/>

==Alpine climber==

Minnigerode was an [[Alpine climbing|Alpine climber]] and a member of the Basel section of the [[Swiss Alpine Club]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnigerode, Bernhard (1837-1896) |url=https://kalliope-verbund.info/de/eac?eac.id=117048410 |website=Kalliope-Verbund |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref> One of the couloirs on the East face of the [[Ortler]] was named after Minnigerode following his first attempted climb in 1878. For further details of Minnigerode's climbing achievements see [[:it:Baptist Bernhard von Minnigerode|it:Bernhard Minnigerode]].

==Honours==

Minnigerode was elected as a corresponding member of the mathematical class of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] in 1874.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Verzeichniss der Mitglieder der Konigl. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Gottingen |trans-title=List of members of the Royal Society of Sciences in Gottingen |journal=Abhandlungen der Königlichen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen |year=1882 |volume=29 |page=xviii |url=https://archive.org/details/abhandlungender14gtgoog/page/XVIII/mode/2up |access-date=2 August 2025 |language=German}}</ref>
